meta_jurisdiction_context.legal_system_doctrine: Civil Law (codified continental system based on the Luxembourg Civil Code, Commercial Code and the Law of 10 August 1915 on Commercial Companies, as amended; direct application of EU regulations and directives)

ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Law of 10 August 1915 on Commercial Companies, as amended (SARL rules, notarial incorporation at Arts. 180 et seq.); Law of 12 November 2004 on the fight against money laundering and terrorist financing, as amended, including the Law of 25 March 2020 transposing Directive (EU) 2018/843; Law of 13 January 2019 establishing the Register of Beneficial Owners ('RBE'); CSSF Regulation No 12-02 of 14 December 2012 on AML/CFT, as amended; CSSF Circular 18/698 on the authorisation and organisation of Alternative Investment Fund Managers; CSSF Circular 17/650 on sanctions and AML/CFT internal controls.
ubo_and_aml_profiling.ubo_disclosure_level: Government_Only_Access — The RBE register is accessible to the Luxembourg Financial Intelligence Unit (CRF), CSSF, CAA, judicial authorities, notaries, lawyers and bailiffs and to natural or legal persons demonstrating a legitimate interest; unrestricted public access was restricted following the CJEU judgments of 22 November 2022 (C-37/20 and C-601/20) and the implementing Luxembourg legislative amendments.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certified true copy of the passport of each shareholder, manager, director and ultimate beneficial owner
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Passport authority or consulate of the country of nationality; for Luxembourg residents, the municipal administration may certify copies
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille (1961 Convention) where the issuing state is a party; otherwise Consular Legalization through the competent Luxembourg embassy or consulate

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of good conduct (extrait de casier judiciaire / police clearance certificate) for each manager, director and UBO
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: National criminal records authority of each UBO's country of residence
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille for member states of the 1961 Convention; otherwise Consular Legalization via Luxembourg diplomatic mission

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Proof of residential address (recent utility bill or bank statement) for each UBO, manager and director
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Utility provider or licensed bank in the UBO's country of residence
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille or, for non-Convention states, Consular Legalization; Luxembourg notary may accept certified translations with original verification

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Bank reference letter from an established bank confirming the professional and financial standing of each UBO and founder
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Licensed commercial bank of the UBO or founder
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille or Consular Legalization; bank signature verified by apostille certificate where required by the nominated Luxembourg notary

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of incorporation, registered office certificate, register excerpt and constitutional documents of any foreign corporate shareholder or corporate director
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Official company registry of the foreign jurisdiction of incorporation
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille for Convention members; otherwise Consular Legalization by Luxembourg consular authorities

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certified corporate resolutions and power of attorney authorizing representatives to execute the Luxembourg notarial incorporation deed
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Board of directors or corporate secretary of the foreign corporate shareholder or appointing entity
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille or Consular Legalization, followed by certified translation into French or German

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory pre-incorporation screening of all shareholders, managers, directors, UBOs and authorized signatories against the EU Consolidated Financial Sanctions List, UN Security Council sanctions resolutions, OFAC SDN and Non-SDN lists, the Luxembourg Ministry of Finance consolidated sanctions database and FATF jurisdiction watchlists; PEP identification and enhanced due diligence must be performed in accordance with the Law of 12 November 2004 and CSSF Regulation No 12-02; screening results must be documented in the incorporation KYC file, refreshed at signature of the notarial deed, and any positive hit requires escalation to the MLRO and termination of the engagement pending authoritative clearance.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Luxembourg Business Registers ('LBR') online platform at www.lbr.lu and the RCS (Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés) module of the official eJustice portal at justice.public.lu; name availability searches and reservations are filed through the LBR e-portal by the designated Luxembourg notary or counsel on behalf of the founders.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: The company name may be expressed in any language provided it is written in Latin characters; accents and diacritical marks are permissible but ASCII transliteration is recommended for registry searchability; the mandatory legal-form suffix must appear in French, either in full as 'Société à Responsabilité Limitée' or by the recognized abbreviation 'S.à r.l.' / 'SARL'; the full name must be distinguishable from all existing RCS entries and must not be misleading as to the company's activity or legal form; on all official documents the name must be accompanied by the French legal-form suffix.
prohibited_and_sensitive_tokens: Banque / Bank / Bankier — reserved for credit institutions holding a CSSF license under the Law of 5 April 1993
Assurance / Insurance / Réassurance — reserved for undertakings supervised by the Commissariat aux Assurances (CAA)
Fonds / Fund / SICAV / SIF / RAIF / FCP — reserved for CSSF-regulated collective investment vehicles
Bourse / Stock Exchange / Marché Réglementé — reserved for licensed exchange and trading venue operators
Université / University / Académie — protected terms subject to ministry authorization
Croix-Rouge / Red Cross / Geneva cross and other protected emblems under the Geneva Conventions Act
Société Anonyme / SA / SCA / SE — misleading references to another corporate form and therefore prohibited for an SARL unless adopted under the correct corporate form

Luxembourg / Lëtzebuerg / City of Luxembourg — protected under the special statutory regime for the name 'Luxembourg'; requires prior ministerial authorization and proof that the registered office is located in Luxembourg
Any name contrary to public order or good morals, or misleading as to the company's object, nationality or legal form under the Law of 10 August 1915, as amended
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: The name reservation submitted through LBR is valid for an initial period of 30 days and may be extended once for a further 30 days upon payment of an additional statutory reservation fee; after the maximum 60-day period, priority lapses and the name returns to the pool. If the LBR/RCS rejects the proposed name, the rejection grounds are notified electronically; counsel must within 15 days file a formal administrative objection with the RCS, simultaneously reserving two or three alternative names to preserve priority. If the objection is dismissed or the rejection is based on a third-party prior right, the applicant may initiate proceedings before the commercial chamber of the Tribunal d'arrondissement de Luxembourg, with service of process within 30 days of the refusal; a successful judgment restores the name reservation for a new 30-day period, failing which the applicant proceeds under the approved alternative name.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: A pure virtual, letterbox or shared-registered-agent address without genuine physical presence in Luxembourg is not permissible for a venture-capital general partner: the SARL must maintain its statutory seat ('siège statutaire') at a real physical address in Luxembourg, and because the entity will carry on licensed activity as an AIFM or as manager of a RAIF or SIF under CSSF supervision, it must demonstrate substantive local presence — dedicated premises, Luxembourg-based management, board meeting capacity and available staff. A virtual or registered-office arrangement may at most be used for a short transitional period pending installation of the permanent registered office; the CSSF will treat a letterbox establishment as a critical deficiency in the licensing and fit-and-proper assessment.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Medium-High — estimated 30-45% annual probability of an unannounced physical on-site inspection by the CSSF or the Luxembourg Financial Intelligence Unit (CRF) once the GP commences regulated activity; the probability rises above 60% during the first 18 months following authorization as part of the CSSF's risk-based supervisory cycle for AIFMs managing third-party capital.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Luxembourg notary (notaire) appointed by the founders
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Statutory notarial fee schedule applied to the minimum share capital of EUR 12,000; prevailing Luxembourg market benchmark of EUR 900–1,500, exclusive of VAT

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Company name availability search and statutory name reservation through LBR
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: LBR statutory fee tariff for name reservation, approximately EUR 19 per reservation

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: RCS registration of the SARL and deposit of the notarial incorporation deed
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: RCS statutory fee schedule: EUR 75 registration fee plus EUR 19 document deposit fee

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Apostille and consular legalization processing fees for foreign corporate and personal documents

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Cost-recovery basis; official apostille and consular certificate fees billed at actual cost

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Certified translation of foreign notarial, corporate and personal documents into French or German

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: CSSF published annual fee schedule; one-off application contribution, subject to the CSSF final invoice

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Professional registered-office provider or law firm offering substance services in Luxembourg
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Prevailing market rate for a substance-ready office package comprising physical address, meeting room access and compliance support for the first operational year

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Luxembourg Law of 10 August 1915 on Commercial Companies, as amended - Articles 710-1 to 710-19 (SARL regime) together with Articles 1, 11-14 and 36 (formation, defectivity and nullity); Law of 19 December 2002 on the Register of Commerce and Companies (RCS) and annual accounts; Law of 2 September 2011 regulating access to professions; Law of 12 July 2013 on alternative investment fund managers, as applicable.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR) - Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés (RCS), Grand-Duché de Luxembourg
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Notarial Deed of Incorporation (Acte constitutif) and Articles of Association (Statuts) filed electronically by the Luxembourg notary with the RCS via the eFormalités portal (Form C1), accompanied by the capital blocking certificate
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: Statutory minimum subscribed capital EUR 12,000; cash contributions must be credited to a blocked account at a Luxembourg credit institution before the deed is signed, with at least 25% of the nominal value of each cash share and 100% of any share premium paid in; contributions in kind must be fully released and covered by a réviseur d'entreprises agréé report; the funds remain blocked until the RCS registration certificate issues.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED: 1. That the founders' share subscription and the contribution of share capital to the société's blocked bank account are hereby ratified, and the certificate of capital deposit issued by [Bank] is acknowledged. 2. That the company's registered office is fixed at [Address], Luxembourg, and the documents evidencing the domiciliation agreement are approved. 3. That [Name] is appointed sole gérant (manager) with sole signatory power and full authority to represent the company to third parties. 4. That the gérant is delegated to file all statutory documents with the Trade and Companies Register, complete RESA and CSSF/licensing filings, and procure operational permits.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Name reservation and preliminary RCS screening
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR) - RCS online denomination reservation (rcs.lu / eFormalités)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit the demande de réservation de dénomination for the proposed corporate name 'XYZ SARL'; LBR checks distinctiveness and public-policy compatibility; the reservation is valid for two months; forward the reservation certificate to the notary before deed drafting.
required_dossiers: Copy of founder's passport or corporate extract
Power of attorney if filed by a third party
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name is rejected for confusing similarity, immediately re-file with a second-priority name; an administrative appeal against refusal may be lodged with the RCS registrar within 15 days.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Drafting of the articles of association and the notarial deed
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Chambre des Notaires du Grand-Duché de Luxembourg (instrumenting notary)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Instruct the notary with the reserved name, registered office address, corporate purpose covering venture-capital GP services, share capital of at least EUR 12,000, shareholder identities and proposed gérant(s); the notary prepares the statuts and the acte constitutif; any in-kind contribution requires a réviseur d'entreprises agréé valuation report.
required_dossiers: KYC documents for all shareholders and UBOs
Auditor's report on any in-kind contribution
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the notary queries the corporate purpose as unlawful or too broad, amend the draft before signature; if AML/KYC documentation is incomplete under the Law of 12 November 2004, supplement the beneficial-ownership chain and source-of-funds evidence.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Opening of a blocked capital account and deposit of share capital
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Luxembourg credit institution selected by the founders (e.g., BIL, BGL BNP Paribas, Spuerkeess)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Open a compte de souscription bloqué in the future company's name; each shareholder wires the cash contribution from a personal or corporate account; the bank issues an attestation de blocage confirming receipt and blocking until RCS registration; funds must not be withdrawn before registration.
required_dossiers: Draft statutes and corporate KYC file
Source-of-funds documentation for shareholders and UBOs
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the bank refuses for AML/KYC reasons, remediate with enhanced source-of-funds documentation and a detailed fund business plan, or transfer the deposit to another Luxembourg credit institution; the blocked balance must cover EUR 12,000 plus any share premium.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Execution of the notarial deed of incorporation
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: The founders and the appointed gérant(s) appear before the notary and sign the acte constitutif; the notary verifies the attestation de blocage and KYC documents, records the deed, and delivers an expédition (certified copy) for the subsequent RCS filing.
required_dossiers: Final notarial deed and articles (for signature)
Identity papers of all signatories and gérants
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If a signatory cannot appear in person, use a notarised power of attorney or permitted videoconference execution; material errors in the deed are cured by an acte rectificatif signed before the same notary prior to registration.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Electronic registration with the RCS and issuance of the registration certificate
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés (RCS) - LBR eFormalités portal
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: The notary files the inscription électronique (Form C1) with the scanned notarial deed and proof of payment of registry fees; the RCS allocates the national business number (matricule) and issues the registration extract; legal personality is acquired upon registration.
required_dossiers: Proof of payment of registry and publication fees
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the RCS raises a query, respond within the eight-day correction deadline; a formal refusal can be appealed to the Tribunal d'arrondissement under the Law of 19 December 2002.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Recueil électronique des sociétés et associations (RESA) and the Register of Beneficial Owners (RBE) - LBR
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Arrange RESA publication of the deed within one month of RCS registration; file the RBE declaration within one month identifying the ultimate natural-person owners and their ownership percentages.
required_dossiers: RBE declaration form with supporting identity documents
Organisational chart of the venture-capital fund structure
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Late RESA publication affects opposability to third parties but is cured by immediate publication; RBE non-compliance triggers administrative fines up to EUR 1,250,000, cured by a complete corrective RBE filing.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Business establishment permit, VAT, social security and CSSF/licensing registrations
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Ministère de l'Économie - Direction Générale des PME; Administration de l'enregistrement, des domaines et de la TVA (AEDT); Centre Commun de la Sécurité Sociale (CCSS); Commission de Surveillance du Secteur Financier (CSSF)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Apply for the Autorisation d'établissement using the RCS extract and proof of managers' professional qualification and good repute; register for VAT via Form 10; enrol employees with the CCSS within eight days; if acting as a full-scope AIFM, submit a separate CSSF authorisation application under the Law of 12 July 2013 (statutory review up to six months).
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Autorisation d'établissement is refused, request the reasoned decision and appeal to the Tribunal Administratif within three months; if CSSF authorisation is refused, re-file with a corrected compliance programme or opt for registered-AIFM status.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Ministère de l'Économie - Direction Générale des PME for the establishment permit; Commission de Surveillance du Secteur Financier (CSSF) for AIFM authorisation or registration under the Law of 12 July 2013
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Autorisation d'établissement (establishment licence under the Law of 2 September 2011) and/or CSSF AIFM authorisation as a registered or full-scope alternative investment fund manager

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Administration de l'environnement - Ministère de l'Environnement, du Climat et de la Biodiversité
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Class 3 - no full EIA required: administrative office use is not listed in the EIA categories of the Law of 15 May 2018; only a municipal classement notification for the premises is required
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Wastewater discharge to the municipal sewer must respect municipal sewer limits and the Luxembourg water framework law; no IED permit applies to office premises; waste, WEEE and e-waste must be handled by approved collectors under EU Directive 2012/19/EU

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire-safety inspection and clearance by the Service d'Incendie et de Secours (SIDS); structural load verification for server, archive and storage rooms; occupational health and safety clearance by the Inspection du Travail et des Mines (ITM) and employer registration with the Association d'assurance accident (AAA).

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Administration des contributions directes (ACD) – Luxembourg direct tax authority; portal: MyGuichet.lu (https://myguichet.lu). Administration de l'enregistrement, des domaines et de la TVA (AEDT) – Luxembourg indirect tax and duties authority; VAT registration, filings and rulings administered through MyGuichet.lu and the dedicated eTVA / EDES electronic applications.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: On incorporation, every Luxembourg SARL is registered with the Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés (RCS), and the Luxembourg direct tax administration issues a single business reference number (matricule) used for corporate income tax (CIT), municipal business tax (MBT), and net wealth tax (NWT) purposes. The VAT identification number is applied for separately from the AEDT via form 640 (electronic filing on MyGuichet.lu). For a foreign entity without a Luxembourg seat, the AEDT requires a direct VAT registration application, accompanied by proof of existence, a certificate of fiscal domicile from the home jurisdiction, details of intended Luxembourg taxable activities, and, where applicable, evidence of a local fiscal representative. No hard turnover threshold applies; registration is due before the first taxable transaction. Upon approval, a LU-prefixed VAT number is assigned; processing normally completes within two weeks.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: Luxembourg does not have a check-the-box election. An SARL is irrebuttably opaque and fully taxable in its own name. The principal statutory elections available are: (a) fiscal unity for income and municipal business tax under Article 164bis LIR, elective for a direct or indirect 95%-owned vertical group; (b) VAT grouping under Article 60 of the VAT Law, creating a single taxable person for Luxembourg VAT purposes; (c) the participation exemption under Article 166 LIR, applied where the holding reaches the statutory threshold (10% shareholding or EUR 1,200,000 acquisition cost) and the shares are held for at least 12 months, exempting qualifying dividends and capital gains; and (d) foreign entity classification mismatches are managed under the ATAD anti-hybrid rules, which do not permit taxpayer-driven filing elections.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Value Added Tax (VAT) – taxe sur la valeur ajoutée (TVA) – governed by the Luxembourg VAT Law of 12 February 1979 and the EU VAT Directive (2006/112/EC).
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: EUR 30,000 (annual turnover small-business exemption for Luxembourg-established businesses); EUR 10,000 (intra-Community distance-sales registration threshold for foreign EU suppliers); otherwise mandatory VAT registration from the first taxable supply in Luxembourg.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Luxembourg neither operates real-time fiscal clearance nor requires B2B e-invoicing or digital stamping. E-invoicing is legally valid; all invoices must be preserved for at least ten years. B2G e-invoices to the Luxembourg central administration must be submitted via the PEPPOL network in compliance with European standard EN 16931 (using CIUS EDI/UBL/UBL invoice profile). VAT returns and EC sales lists must be e-filed through MyGuichet.lu; no transactional API reporting is currently mandated.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: To zero-rate exports of goods, the supplier (whether established in Luxembourg or not) must prove: (i) the goods were sold to a purchaser outside the EU; (ii) the goods physically left the EU, generally within 90 days of dispatch (or within a reasonable period, with customs endorsement); (iii) possession of a definitive customs export declaration and transport documents evidencing exit from the EU; (iv) the supply was taxable in Luxembourg but for the exemption (i.e., place-of-supply rules point to Luxembourg); and (v) commercial records linking the invoice, payment, and delivery. Services ancillary to an export (transport, loading/unloading, freight forwarding) qualify for zero rating when directly linked to the export. B2B services to non-EU taxable persons are outside the scope of Luxembourg VAT under the EU place-of-supply rules, so no Luxembourg VAT is due even though they are not technically zero-rated.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (Single Administrative Document or export declaration in the Luxembourg customs IT system)
Bill of Lading, CMR consignment note, CIM rail consignment note, or Air Waybill as applicable
Inward Remittance Certificate or equivalent bank SWIFT credit confirmation evidencing currency receipt
Packing list and delivery / loading note
Transport insurance and forwarding instructions (if available)
Certificate of origin and/or EUR.1 / EUSALTA statement where applicable
Evidence of non-EU purchaser status (e.g., certificate of incorporation, VAT registration certificate or comparable documentation)
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: Luxembourg applies a strict evidentiary burden on the vendor in all export zero-rating claims. The AEDT may demand the full documentation bundle before accepting the 0% rate; if export is not evidenced within the statutory deadlines, VAT is assessed at the standard 17% rate with late-payment interest. The VAT Law imposes administrative penalties for non-compliance, including recurrent daily fines for failure to file and penalties for intentional under-declaration; criminal liability for VAT fraud can reach EUR 125,000 in fines and imprisonment. Ordinary assessment limitation is three years, extended to five years for omitted returns and to ten years for fraudulent conduct. Where fraudulent zero-rating is established, the AEDT retrospectively recharacterizes the supply as taxable and may claw back the VAT for all transactions in the fraudulent scheme, with joint liability applied to any party who knew or should have known of the fraud.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Banque centrale du Luxembourg (BCL) acting as the Eurosystem national central bank; prudential supervision of Luxembourg credit institutions and authorised payment/e-money institutions is exercised by the Commission de Surveillance du Secteur Financier (CSSF). The CSSF applies the EU Single Rulebook (CRR/CRD IV, AMLD4/5, PSD2) and issues binding circulars on money laundering (CSSF Circular 17/650 as amended) and on balance of payments reporting (BCL/CSSF joint framework).
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Full and unrestricted convertibility. Luxembourg is a Eurozone member with no exchange control legislation; capital movements and payments are liberalised under Articles 63–66 TFEU. Capital account inflows (share capital, capital calls, shareholder loans) and outflows (profit distributions, redemption of fund units, loan repayments) require no BCL or CSSF prior authorisation. The only applicable hurdles are (i) the 15% domestic Luxembourg dividend withholding tax on SARL distributions to non-resident corporate shareholders, reducible under EU Parent-Subsidiary Directive or double tax treaties, and (ii) mandatory balance of payments statistical reporting by resident credit institutions to the BCL for cross-border transactions exceeding de minimis thresholds. No prior registration or negative clearance regime applies to FDI in the SARL or to onward investment by the GP.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: Not applicable. Luxembourg imposes no export proceeds surrender, no mandatory conversion ratio, and no statutory repatriation timeline for commercial or financial receipts. The SARL may hold and dispose of foreign currency freely. Cross-border receipts and payments are subject exclusively to (i) BCL balance of payments statistical capture by the resident bank, (ii) EU, UN and OFAC sanctions screening, and (iii) funds origin verification under Luxembourg AML/CFT law (Law of 12 November 2004, as amended by the Law of 25 March 2020).

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.bank_name: HSBC Continental Europe S.A., Luxembourg Branch

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Operational Account / Capital Call Collection Account

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Low to Medium feasibility, subject to strict legal constraints. Luxembourg-licensed electronic money institutions (EMIs) and payment institutions under the Law of 10 November 2009 (implementing PSD2) and supervised by the CSSF may provide operational IBAN accounts, multi-currency receiving capacity and SWIFT-based outbound wires at lower cost and faster onboarding than tier-1 banks. However, for a licensed Venture Capital GP, EMIs are not a viable primary treasury rail because (i) they cannot grant credit, overdrafts or intraday liquidity; (ii) they cannot hold client money within the meaning of the AIFM Law of 12 July 2013 for fund-level capital calls; (iii) institutional LPs commonly reject EMIs in the Management Agreement's bank account covenant; and (iv) CSSF Circular 17/650 AML expectations require the GP to maintain fund flows through a fully prudentially supervised credit institution. Offshore digital EMIs (e.g., UK-authorised or Lithuanian-licensed) are further restricted by the EU 'passporting' rules and by Luxembourg banks' correspondent due diligence on foreign EMIs. Recommended architecture: tier-1 bank as the sole capital call and disbursement account; a CSSF-authorised EMI as a secondary operational bulk-payment account for small expense reimbursements, capped at EUR 50,000 per transaction.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Remote onboarding is legally permissible in Luxembourg where the applicant has not been physically present and the bank applies a qualified remote identification solution (video conference with liveness check plus electronic signature under eIDAS). In practice, leading banks require at least one video KYC interview for the managing director and for each natural person disclosing 25%+ UBO ownership; most among the 'High' viability tier will also mandate one in-person meeting at the Luxembourg branch or at the bank's representative office in the managing director's jurisdiction before the account is activated. Notarised, apostilled board resolutions and signed KYC questionnaires are mandatory; wet-ink signatures are typically insisted upon for SARL opening documents. A CSSF-licensed GP can leverage its authorisation file to waive re-verification of corporate documentary evidence if the banking relationship is opened within 12 months of issuance of the CSSF licence.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Opaque group ownership with non-EU intermediate holding vehicles or unreported discretionary trusts in the UBO chain
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Current Registre des Bénéficiaires Effectifs (RBE) extract of the SARL; full 100% ownership chart down to each ultimate natural person with passport copies; notarised and apostilled articles of association of every stripco; trustee declarations and trust deed summaries where a fiduciary layer exists; and a written AML/CFT shareholder attestation signed by each UBO, each dated within 3 months of application.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Source of funds or source of wealth insufficiency for the initial share capital and for the capital call collection mandate
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Audited (or certified) financial statements of the SARL for the first two periods; bank reference letter from the GP's home jurisdiction bank; three months of bank statements evidencing the capital injection path; signed limited partnership agreement and capital commitment schedules of each LP; and a board minute approving the treasury policy and naming the authorised signatories.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Regulatory status ambiguity concerning the AIFM licence, registration, or the exemption threshold under the Law of 12 July 2013
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Copy of the CSSF authorisation as an alternative investment fund manager, or the CSSF registration confirmation as a sub-threshold AIFM; the CSSF reference number (NUM); notification filed under Article 3(2) of the AIFM Law; the fund's applicable SIF/RAIF/SICAR documentation; and a legal opinion from a Luxembourg ELP-certified law firm on the licensing perimeter.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Adverse media, contested litigation, or negative jam on the GP's principals or on the target technology portfolio
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Third-party due diligence report issued by Dow Jones or Refinitiv on the entity and all UBOs; contemporaneous public statement and legal counsel memorandum addressing each adverse headline; certificate of non-pending insolvency proceedings from the Luxembourg business register; and enforcement records, if any, with a mitigation explanation from an independent auditor.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Sanctions, PEP, or high-risk jurisdiction exposure in the LP base or in the portfolio company acquisition targets
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Signed institution-wide sanctions and PEP screening policy; completed OFAC, EU, UN and Luxembourg 'liste noire' screening results for all UBOs, LPs and target companies; negative screening certificates from a reputable sanctions screening vendor; written confirmation that no Russian, Belarusian, Iranian, North Korean or Syrian nexus exists in the fund's term sheet; and an ongoing monitoring commitment letter.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Tax transparency and profit attribution concerns at the SARL level (substance, CFC, permanent establishment risk)
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Luxembourg tax residency certificate issued by the Administration des contributions directes (ACD); current value added tax registration certificate (TVA); CRS and FATCA registration proof; substance docket proving onshore governance (board meetings, directors' tax residence, signed minutes, key management premises); and, where relevant, the advance pricing agreement or tax ruling issued by the Luxembourg tax authorities.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: All inbound funding must enter through the dedicated capital call and escrow account at the chosen tier-1 Luxembourg bank. For EUR transfers originating within SEPA, route via SEPA Credit Transfer (ISO 20022 pain.001) or via SWIFT MT103 if the remitting LP is outside SEPA or requires faster settlement. For non-EUR transfers (primarily USD, GBP, CHF), use SWIFT MT103 only, with the fund name, LPA date, clause reference, and 'Capital Call Drawdown' specified in field 70 (Remittance Information). The resident bank automatically captures the transaction for BCL balance of payments statistics under the ECB BOP6 classification, using the primary purpose code 'Direct investment – Equity capital' for injections into the SARL's own capital and 'Financial intermediation – Investment fund shares/units' for LP drawdowns into the regulated VC fund vehicle. The GP must instruct the bank to attach purpose code D.04 (or the bank-specific equivalent) and must provide (i) an executed capital commitment schedule per LP, (ii) the fund's banking authorisation resolution, and (iii) a source-of-funds certificate for any single injection above EUR 1,000,000. No prior BCL approval is required, but the bank must receive the beneficiary's full name and IBAN (LU00 BCCL...), and the GP must confirm that neither the remitter nor the underlying investor is a sanctioned or restricted person.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Portfolio investments, follow-on financings, bridge loans, and management fee payments are cleared through the same operational account. Standard clearing rails: (i) SWIFT MT103 for all high-value cross-border wires to portfolio companies and to legal/ advisory counterparties, with the investment SPA/shareholder agreement reference in field 70; (ii) SWIFT MT202 COV when the payment is directed through an intermediary bank for onward credit to the beneficiary's account, ensuring the ordering customer's information is transmitted in compliance with the FATF Recommendation 16 wire transfer rules; (iii) SEPA Credit Transfers for all EUR disbursements within the SEPA zone, including to portfolio companies in Germany, France, Belgium, and the Netherlands; (iv) TARGET2 immediate settlement for intra-day, critical closings above EUR 1,000,000; and (v) Commercial Letters of Credit (UCP 600) or Standby LCs (ISP98) only where the transaction is structured as a deferred payment in an acquisition or bridge financing; these are typically issued on the GP bank's own credit line and are not available against escrow balances. All outbound transfers require the bank to capture the balance of payments purpose code corresponding to the transaction (portfolio investment in non-resident equity for share purchases; management fees under 'management services'; and interest/principal under 'loan and credit operations'). The SARL must retain supporting board-approved investment minutes and the executed transaction documents at the registered office for a minimum of 5 years to satisfy the bank's post-transaction documentation audit.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: EUR/USD deliverable FX forward contracts, tenor up to 12 months, documented under the 1998 ISDA FX and Currency Option Definitions or the 2021 ISDA Master Agreement, available only against a signed FX ISDA or the bank's standard FX terms and credit support annex.

EUR/USD and EUR/GBP FX swaps (swap points executed with one-week to three-month tenors), permissible for treasury working-capital smoothing and for periodic management fee payments, without margining if trade size is below the bank's FX credit line, otherwise subject to two-way collateral.

Cross-currency interest rate swaps (CCS) for medium-term acquisition financing purposes, permissible only where the SARL has an underlying debt facility in EUR and the portfolio asset generates cash flows in USD, with settlement netting performed via the clearing system at the target bank.

Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) restricted to portfolio exposures in emerging-market currencies (e.g., CNY, INR, BRL) where the SARL holds unhedged equity stakes in unlisted technology companies; NDF tenors limited to 6 months and strictly linked to a documented underlying portfolio valuation event, because the Bank cannot settle NDFs without the beneficiary portfolio company's audited valuation data.

Plain vanilla FX options (EUR/USD, EUR/CHF) as permitted premium instruments solely for protecting an executed investment agreement against adverse currency movement between signing and closing, not for speculative use; options require a specific board resolution and prior approval of the bank's foreign exchange desk.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual confirmation of RCS registered data (annual return against the Luxembourg trade register)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR) – Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés (RCS), via eJustice/MyGuichet
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annually within one month of the RCS anniversary reminder letter issued by LBR; any change to registered data must be filed within one month of the event
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Administrative fines up to EUR 5,000 for inaccurate or missing updates; combined with two consecutive years of missing annual accounts, the RCS may initiate administrative strike-off (radiation d'office)

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Deposit of annual accounts (comptes annuels) approved by the shareholders
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR) – RCS, via eJustice deposit portal
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Shareholders' general meeting within six months of financial year-end and deposit with the RCS within one month of approval (calendar-year SARL: approval by 30 June, deposit by 31 July)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Court-ordered compulsory deposit and statutory fine up to EUR 5,000; non-filing for two consecutive financial years triggers administrative strike-off (radiation d'office)

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Combined corporate income tax and net wealth tax return (Model 900)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Administration des contributions directes (ACD), Luxembourg Inland Revenue
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: 30 June of the year following the tax year for calendar-year taxpayers; extension to 31 December for returns e-filed through MyGuichet
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late-filing surcharge (majoration) up to 10% of the net tax due; late-payment interest of 0.6% per month; taxation d'office (estimated assessment) for persistent default

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual UBO confirmation filing in the Register of Beneficial Owners (Registre des bénéficiaires effectifs)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annually during the first quarter, by 31 March; any UBO change (including share transfers) must be filed within 30 days of the event
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Criminal sanctions: imprisonment of 8 days to 6 months and/or fine of EUR 500 to EUR 12,500 per infringement, imposed on the company and/or managing persons (gérants)

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: CSSF annual regulatory reporting and supervision contribution for the licensed venture capital GP/AIFM
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Commission de Surveillance du Secteur Financier (CSSF)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annual financial report within 6 months of financial year-end; AIFM Annex IV periodic reporting per CSSF Circular 18/698 (annual or quarterly depending on AUM); annual supervision levy per CSSF invoice
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Administrative sanctions up to EUR 5,000,000 or 10% of annual turnover under the AIFM Law of 12 July 2013; suspension or revocation of the CSSF authorization; fines and disqualification of approved managers

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Mandatory independent audit by an approved statutory auditor (réviseur d'entreprises agréé) where the SARL exceeds at least two of the three law-of-19-December-2002 criteria — balance sheet total EUR 4.4 million, net turnover EUR 8.8 million, average workforce 50 — and in all cases where the entity is a CSSF-licensed external AIFM/venture capital GP under the AIFM Law of 12 July 2013; an audit must also be installed upon demand of shareholders holding at least 10% of the subscribed capital
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Luxembourg GAAP under the law of 19 December 2002 on commercial registers and annual accounts, as amended (transposing Directive 2013/34/EU); IFRS as endorsed by the EU is permitted; statutory accounts are kept in EUR and filed in French, German, or English

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Under the law of 13 January 2019, the SARL must confirm its beneficial ownership data each year in the electronic RBE during the first quarter (by 31 March); any change in beneficial ownership, including transfers of shares or parts in the SARL, must additionally be filed with the RBE within 30 days of the transaction; the confirmation must be signed by a natural person authorized to bind the company (gérant or authorized delegate)
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of Members (registre des associés; statutory register of parts, holders, and transfers)
Register of Directors/Managers (gérants; RCS-disclosed mandate and appointment records)
Minute Book (procès-verbaux of shareholders' general meetings and management decisions)

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: USD 1,500–3,500 per year (typical registered-office and domiciliation agent services in Luxembourg City)
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 9,000–22,000 per year (typical independent audit fee for a small VC GP SARL by a Luxembourg réviseur d'entreprises agréé; CSSF-regulated entities may exceed the upper bound)

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 17% top-band CIT (15% on first EUR 175,000 taxable income) + 7% solidarity surcharge on CIT + 6.75% municipal business tax (standard Luxembourg City rate) = aggregate headline rate of approximately 24.94%.
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: No statutory tax holiday. Key preferential rules: (1) Participation exemption - 100% exemption for dividends and capital gains on qualifying shareholdings (10% minimum holding or EUR 6,000,000 acquisition price, held 12 months); applicable to carried interest of a corporate VC GP if the fund participation qualifies. (2) IP box - 80% exemption on net qualifying IP income, effective rate approximately 5%. (3) Grandfathered notional interest deduction on new equity. (4) 0% WHT on arm's-length outbound interest and royalties.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Form 500 'Declaration d'impot sur le revenu des collectivites' plus Annex 500D (balance sheet, P&L and participation schedule); filed electronically via the ACD eCDF portal (access also through MyGuichet).
tax_return_filing_anatomy.reporting_frequency: Annual; provisional CIT instalments are payable quarterly on 10 March, 10 June, 10 September and 10 December of the tax year.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Statutory deadline is 31 May of the year following the calendar tax year; the ACD routinely grants an automatic extension to 31 December for returns filed through eCDF. No carryback of tax losses is permitted.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Taxpayer identification - legal name, legal form (SARL), RCS Luxembourg number, address and tax file number.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Insert Luxembourg registration data only; all non-resident shareholders must be disclosed in the annex to the return with country of residence and tax ID.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Accounting period - start and end dates of the financial year.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Calendar-year alignment is recommended; a foreign parent may consolidate the Luxembourg result under its own accounting calendar but the Luxembourg return must follow Luxembourg commercial law.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Tax residence status and elective regimes (e.g., section 164 special holding regime, IP box election).
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Confirm full tax residence in Luxembourg; a non-resident manager or foreign board presence must not create a permanent establishment of the SARL abroad.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Net turnover / operating revenues - VC GP management fees, advisory and capital-call service income.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: All fee income must be booked at arm's length with supporting time-sheets and invoices; cross-border fee remittances to the Cayman/UAE fund require TP analysis.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Other operating income - carried interest allocations, capital gains and dividend income from participation holdings.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Claim the participation exemption on the Annex 500D schedule; evidence the 12-month holding period and 10%/EUR 6,000,000 participation threshold for fund interests.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Deductible operating expenses - salaries, rent, professional fees, compliance and CSSF supervision costs.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Expenses must be real, substantiated and incurred for the Luxembourg business; intercompany charges require TP documentation and substance proof.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Non-deductible add-backs - fines, excessive entertainment, and interest limitation under ATAD rules (30% EBITDA cap).
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Apply the EBITDA interest limitation with group-ratio and equity-escape tests; profit-participating loans may be recharacterized as equity.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Statutory deductions - participation exemption deduction and IP box exemption.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Attach the participation schedule proving that the fund vehicle is a qualifying undertaking subject to tax or assimilated; treaty-protected distribution evidence required.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Tax loss utilisation - deduction of loss carryforwards from prior years within the 17-year window.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Maintain continuity of economic identity; a change of ownership or cessation of activity may forfeit the carryforward in a cross-border restructuring.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Computation - CIT at the 15%/17% band, 7% solidarity surcharge, municipal business tax at communal rate.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Compute the municipal business tax at the commune of the registered office (Luxembourg City 6.75%); the MBT is deductible for CIT purposes.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Cross-reference to net wealth tax - separate Form 960 filing and minimum net wealth tax of EUR 3,210.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Net wealth tax is due even if CIT is zero; LPs' capital commitments are not treated as equity for NWT unless formally subscribed.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Related-party transactions and BEPS Action 13 TP disclosure - intercompany services, loans, fee and carried-interest flows.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: File Master File/Local File when thresholds are met; disclose the Cayman fund relationship, the ultimate beneficial owner of the GP and any PEs.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing: administrative censure and estimated assessment, mandatory late-payment interest of 0.8% per month (9.6% annual), negligence penalty of up to 10% of understated tax, and intentional evasion penalty of up to 100% plus criminal fine up to EUR 250,000; directors are jointly and severally liable for culpable failure to file.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Form 510 (CbC report notification) and CbC XML report as required by the Luxembourg law of 23 December 2016 implementing EU Directive 2016/881; filed through eCDF.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.reporting_frequency: Annual - CbC notification due by the last day of the reporting fiscal year; CbC report due within 12 months after the reporting fiscal year end.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Notification Form 510: no later than 31 December of the reporting fiscal year. CbC report: within 12 months of the fiscal year end (surrogate filing may extend under the CbC Competent Authority Agreement).

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Reporting fiscal year and constituent entity identification (name, tax ID, jurisdiction).
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Identify the ultimate parent (e.g., Cayman master fund or LP structure) and confirm whether the Luxembourg SARL is an agent/GP or a constituent entity.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Reporting role - Ultimate Parent Entity, Surrogate Parent Entity, or Constituent Entity obliged to file locally.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: If the Cayman parent has no filing obligation, Luxembourg may require the SARL to file a local CbC report; confirm under the relevant qualifying-competent-agreement.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Consolidated group revenue and per-jurisdiction allocation indicators.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Use the group's audited consolidation figures; keep a permanent file with the master file, local file and transfer pricing study.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Failure to file Form 510 or CbC report: administrative fine up to EUR 25,000 per omission; intentional non-compliance exposed to criminal penalties (fine up to EUR 150,000 and imprisonment up to 4 years); ACD may issue an estimated assessment.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 15% domestic dividend withholding tax; reduced to 0% under the participation exemption (10% shareholding or EUR 6,000,000 acquisition price held for 12 months) and 0% under the EU Parent-Subsidiary Directive for qualifying EU corporate recipients.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: Luxembourg has no DTA with the Cayman Islands; relief is therefore structured through the EU Parent-Subsidiary Directive or by locating the fund in a treaty jurisdiction. Procedure: (1) obtain a Luxembourg ACD tax residence attestation for the SARL; (2) the outbound distribution payer applies relief-at-source by filing a request with the ACD including: beneficiary ownership certificate, TRC issued by the recipient's residence state (apostilled), shareholding register and a substance/PPT self-certification; (3) refund claims for excessive WHT must be filed within 5 years; the ACD applies the Principal Purpose Test under the law of 21 December 2017 before granting treaty or Directive relief.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Outbound interest to non-residents: 0% WHT on arm's-length interest (no domestic interest WHT; profit-participating loans may be recharacterized as equity at 15% dividend WHT). Outbound royalties: 0% WHT (Luxembourg abolished royalty withholding tax). Under selected DTAs, interest ranges 0-10% and royalties 0-5%; Cayman is outside the treaty network, so treaty benefits for Cayman LPs are unavailable and Luxembourg substance is essential to avoid 15% WHT leakage.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: EUR 450,000 - Local File obligation for the Luxembourg entity when aggregate related-party transactions exceed EUR 450,000 in a fiscal year; Master File and CbC Report obligation when the consolidated group revenue reaches EUR 750,000,000.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Luxembourg does not operate a Gulf-style ESR code, but economic substance is enforced through: (1) ATAD GAAR (law of 21 December 2017) recharacterizing artificial arrangements lacking commercial reality; (2) LIR Article 166 anti-abuse exception denying the participation exemption where the GP is a 'letterbox'; (3) AIFMD substance requirements for an authorized VC GP (two Luxembourg-based directors, physical registered office, investment decisions made in Luxembourg, delegated functions restricted to regulated delegates); (4) ACD Circular LIR No. 56/1 minimum substance guidance. The GP must demonstrate payroll, premises, board meetings, and compliance/KYC functions in Luxembourg to support treaty access and 0% dividend WHT.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Intentional omission of carried interest or management fee income from Form 500; falsification of investor registers; creation of fabricated invoices to inflate deductible expenses; hidden foreign bank accounts.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Penalty of 100% of the evaded CIT; mandatory late-payment interest at 0.8% per month; criminal fine up to EUR 250,000 and imprisonment of 5 to 10 years for natural persons; corporate dissolution is possible in aggravated cases.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors are jointly and severally liable for the evaded tax and civil restitution of diverted assets; travel bans (restriction on leaving the Schengen area); criminal imprisonment for the masterminding director.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Shell Company / Letterbox and GAAR (Abus de Droit)
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Maintaining a Luxembourg SARL as VC GP with no real staff, no office, no board minutes and no local decision-making while investment decisions are taken in Cayman/UAE; artificial round-tripping of management fees.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: ACD recharacterization under the ATAD GAAR; denial of participation exemption and treaty benefits; retroactive CIT at a combined 24.94% rate plus re-grossed 15% dividend WHT; negligence penalty of 10%; CSSF revocation of the AIFM/RAIF license.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors may be held liable for unpaid corporate taxes when the entity is deemed a sham; criminal exposure for 'gestion frauduleuse'; professional disqualification and refusal of future CSSF fit-and-proper approvals.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Non-arm's-length management fees charged to the fund or portfolio companies; incorrect benchmark selection under TNMM; failure to prepare Local File despite intercompany transactions over EUR 450,000; missing CbC notification Form 510.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: ACD adjustment to the arm's-length price; negligence penalty up to 10% (up to 100% for deliberate mispricing); interest at 0.8% per month; documentation fines up to EUR 25,000; risk of economic double taxation and secondary adjustments.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Director sign-off liability for inaccurate statutory accounts; characterization as 'fraude a la loi' piercing the corporate veil; civil exposure to LPs for inflated tax leakage and audit costs.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: AML/CFT and KYC Violations (VC GP Specific)
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Failure to conduct KYC/AML checks on LP capital-call wires; failure to register as an AIFM/RAIF with the CSSF; processing investments from sanctioned or PEP-linked investors through the GP's payment rails.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Under the Luxembourg law of 12 November 2004 (as amended): money-laundering imprisoned 5 to 10 years; fines up to EUR 250,000 for natural persons or EUR 1,250,000 for legal persons; CSSF administrative fines up to EUR 5,000,000 or 10% of annual turnover; license revocation and public censure.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: The AML compliance officer and managing director face personal criminal liability; travel bans and asset freezes; confiscation orders against personal assets; prohibition from holding management positions in regulated entities.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Acting as general partner and exercising de facto management of a venture capital fund (capital calls, portfolio selection, divestment, distribution) without authorization under the AIFM Law of 12 July 2013 or the RAIF Law of 23 July 2016.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Criminal penalties under the AIFM Law: imprisonment and fines; all management agreements rendered void; CSSF injunctions and winding-up orders; retroactive reassessment of the GP's income with 15% dividend WHT exposure.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Each participating director is personally liable for damages to investors; prohibition from company management for up to 10 years; extradition alerts triggered in cross-border criminal proceedings.
